title: Corey Haines' Social Content playbook: story first, specific hooks, repurposing, no AI tells
summary: Corey Haines' open-source social media skill for AI agents. It puts storytelling above platform tactics, then covers hooks, content pillars, repurposing long-form into atoms, engagement routines, short-form video structure, and stripping AI tells from posts.

principles.text: Storytelling and audience connection come before platform tactics or algorithm tricks.
principles.quote: storytelling and connecting with your audience come first. The better the user can share their story, the better their posts will perform

principles.text: The first line decides whether the post gets read, so spend your effort on the hook.
principles.quote: The first line determines whether anyone reads the rest.

principles.text: Hook formulas are only shapes. Fill them with a specific fact, number, or story, and cut AI tells.
principles.quote: A hook formula is a starting shape. Fill it with a specific fact, number, or story.

principles.text: Generated-sounding posts get scrolled past and called out. Avoid contrast reveals, broetry, and engagement bait.
principles.quote: Readers scroll past posts that read as generated, and on LinkedIn they say so in the comments.

principles.text: Build content from pillar pieces and extract atoms for each platform instead of starting from scratch.
principles.quote: The best social content isn't created from scratch — it's extracted from longer-form pillar content and adapted to each platform.

principles.text: Organize content around 3-5 pillars tied to your expertise, and engage consistently with 20-50 accounts in your space.
principles.quote: Build your content around 3-5 pillars that align with your expertise and audience interests.
